extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and prosecution teams filing or prosecuting Israeli patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on requesting and meeting requirements for Modified Examination at the Israel Patent Office — i.e., expedited examination based on one or two corresponding foreign patents and the procedural/eligibility conditions and strategic considerations that apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible jurisdictions for corresponding patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding patent must originate from one of a specified list of foreign jurisdictions for Modified Examination to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed eligible jurisdictions include: Australia, Austria, USA, Germany, Denmark, UK, Russian Federation, Japan, EPO, Norway, Canada, and Sweden. Note: a US continuation or continuation-in-part (CIP) patent may qualify provided no prior publication related to the same patent family occurred before the Israeli application's priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single or two corresponding patents allowed (single invention requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified Examination can be requested based on either a single corresponding patent or two corresponding patents, but the combined claims must refer to a single invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors PCT and EP practice: if two corresponding patents are used, their claim sets must together concern only one invention (unity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be identical to corresponding patent (except non-acceptable claim types removed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Israeli claims must be identical to those of the corresponding patent, with claims that are not acceptable under Israeli law removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of non-acceptable claim types under Israeli law include omnibus claims and therapeutic method claims; such claims should be removed prior to using Modified Examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common priority date and support by priority document
rubrics_metrics.description: The Israeli application and the corresponding patent must share a common priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The common priority may come from the Israeli application, the corresponding patent, or a third application that both claim. In cases of multiple priority claims, Modified Examination is possible only if the claim set is supported by the common priority document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict applicant identity requirement (with limited exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A strict interpretation requires that the applicants of the Israeli application and of the corresponding application that led to the granted corresponding patent be identical individuals or entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While strict alignment is preferred, exceptions may be permitted—particularly if the corresponding patent was granted or assigned to the Israeli applicant. Applicants should verify applicant/assignee alignment or be prepared to justify exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of corresponding patent copy and translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit a copy of the corresponding patent when requesting Modified Examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the corresponding patent is not in English, an English translation should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description and drawings must match or meet Israeli requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The description and drawings in the Israeli application should match those of the corresponding patent or otherwise meet Israeli formal/substantive requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the specification and figures are consistent with the corresponding patent and that any differences still comply with Israeli disclosure and formal requirements to avoid objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims dependency preservation when reducing claim count
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified Examination may be requested with a reduced number of claims, but claim dependency relationships must remain unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can streamline the claim set for Modified Examination, provided that dependencies among retained claims are preserved; avoid altering dependency structure in ways that would change claim scope relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s discretion to raise special objections
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission of a Modified Examination request, the Examiner retains authority to object to the request on specific grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special grounds may include situations where known prior art was not considered during the foreign examination. The Examiner can therefore require further examination or refuse to accept the Modified Examination route if such issues exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement for adverse proceedings against corresponding patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If the corresponding patent undergoes adverse proceedings (opposition, revocation, re‑examination) before the Israeli application's grant, the Patent Office must be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notification may cause the Israeli application to return to regular examination rather than remain on the Modified Examination track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of meeting patentability provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent granted via Modified Examination is presumed to meet various patentability provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum lists presumptions including novelty, inventive step, unity of the invention, sufficiency of disclosure, and support of the claims by the description. Applicants should be aware this is a presumption tied to the corresponding patent and may have strategic implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic downside: alignment with corresponding patent limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Modified Examination may cause the Israeli patent to align with restrictions or limitations found in the corresponding patent, potentially narrowing scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider whether acceptance of corresponding-patent claim scope is appropriate, especially if broader claim scope in Israel is desired. Modified Examination expedites prosecution but can limit claim breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advised caution if relevant prior art was not considered abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are advised against seeking Modified Examination if relevant prior art was not considered during examination of the corresponding patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If important prior art was overlooked in the foreign prosecution, the Israeli Examiner may raise objections or the application may be returned to regular examination — reducing the benefit of expedited processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: when to request Modified Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified Examination can be requested at any stage before acceptance of the Israeli application, but timing affects practicality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically recommended to request Modified Examination before substantive examination begins, often in response to an Official Notification Prior to Examination, to maximize chances of an expedited and smooth process.
